title: Brother Lawrence's conversations
hook: he trained himself to return to God's presence whenever he forgot
tomorrow: how little can a prayer be and still count?

segments.voice: Yesterday a broom, and Herbert's clause: as for thee. Who sweeps a room that way makes that and the action fine. Today, someone who lived inside that idea, in a kitchen.

You meant to check one thing on your phone. Forty minutes later you surface, not sure where the time went. Or you start the day promising to be patient, and by lunch you've forgotten you promised. Forgetting isn't a rare failure. It's the default setting. So what do you do about it? A cook in a French monastery kept forgetting God all day long, and a visitor wrote down what he did.
screen: `FORTY MINUTES, GONE.` → `FORGETTING IS THE DEFAULT.` → `A COOK WHO KEPT FORGETTING.`

segments.voice: He's known as Brother Lawrence, a lay brother of the Carmelites, the same order as Teresa and John. He wasn't a priest or a scholar. In the conversations a visitor named Joseph de Beaufort wrote down, Lawrence calls himself, in effect, a clumsy fellow who broke things. They put him to work in the kitchen, a job he says he naturally disliked. And there he set himself one practice: to keep turning to God, in the middle of the work, as to a friend in the room. Here's the part people skip. He failed at it, constantly. So what did he do when he noticed he'd drifted? According to the conversations, he didn't punish himself or start a stricter program. He simply admitted it to God, in effect: this is what I do when I'm left to myself; you'll have to keep me from falling. Then he gave it no more worry, and turned back. And again. And again. Over time, he said, the hours of work and the hours of prayer stopped feeling different. One to tell a friend tonight: he said that in the clatter of the kitchen, with several people calling for different things at once, he could be as calm with God as on his knees in chapel.
screen: `A LAY BROTHER IN A KITCHEN.` · `HE FORGOT, CONSTANTLY.` · `ADMIT IT, NO FUSS.` · `TURN BACK. AND AGAIN.` · then, large: `RETURN, AND RETURN.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and choose one anchor: the word here, or a name of God if you pray. When your mind wanders, and it will, notice it without scolding and come back to the anchor. The returns are the practice, not the stillness.
Brother Lawrence's conversations. A kitchen worker's habit, written down by a visitor: notice you've drifted, admit it plainly, come back.
Your line: return, and return. Lawrence never stopped forgetting; he just never stopped coming back. Day 1657, kept.

screen: `DAY 1657 COUNTS.` → `SAINTS AND TEACHERS IN THEIR OWN WORDS · 56 OF 80.` → `TOMORROW: HOW LITTLE CAN A PRAYER BE AND STILL COUNT?`

howItsDone: Brother Lawrence's conversations and letters, gathered as The Practice of the Presence of God, are read by Christians of many churches; readers try to turn to God briefly in the middle of ordinary work.

fork.setup: you promised yourself to keep God in mind through a long shift at work. at lunch you realize you forgot all morning. what would Lawrence do?
options: admit it plainly, without fuss, and turn back right then.
write the day off and start over tomorrow with a stricter plan.
make up for the lost morning with an hour of prayer tonight.
fork.reveal: no penalty, no new program. he owned the drift in a sentence and came back, as many times as it took.

chat.says: Pop's PT: same 10 steps, over and over. he's grumpy. and i forget to pray for him till 11pm. fail?
options: Not a fail. Brother Lawrence forgot all the time; he just came back, no drama.
Kinda. Set five alarms, and if you miss one, make it up with a longer prayer.
Once a day is plenty. Praying all day long is for monks, not for students.
chat.meaning: Lawrence didn't punish himself for forgetting; he turned back each time he noticed. Like Pop's steps, the repeating is the training.
